selection.rule: least recently reviewed with rotation-order tie break

pue.boundary: Meta annual data-center fleet; best-available inputs may include internal meters, design estimates and utility bills. It is not isolated to Q2 2026 AI training, inference, third-party cloud or the future Hyperion and El Paso ventures.
pue.basis: Meta reported annual data-center PUE of 1.08. The report defines PUE as data-center energy divided by IT electricity load. Because fleet/site IT-energy weights and a Q2 2026 AI-workload boundary are not disclosed, 1.08 is retained as a historical fleet proxy and is not applied to the revenue model.
pue.aggregation_rule: Use IT-energy-weighted PUE only after matching site or cohort IT energy and PUE are disclosed.

model.revenue_scope: Incremental recognized advertising or engagement monetization attributable to AI plus recognized external Meta Compute revenue; exclude total advertising revenue, non-AI advertising growth, Reality Labs hardware and prospective compute offers
model.capacity_time_basis: 91-day quarter; reconstruct opening active AI IT MW plus additions and retirements weighted by active days, then integrate physical utilization over the same period

assumptions.basis: Simple annualization of one quarter; diagnostic only and not a forecast.
The FY2024 fleet PUE has a broader and older perimeter than Q2 2026 AI compute, so it is not substituted into the model.
No physical-utilization definition or measured range is disclosed. The algebraic 1/utilization relationship is retained without inventing cases.
Issuer calls the campus 1 GW of compute capacity but does not define whether this is utility, facility or IT load. It is used only for explicitly labeled stated-capacity financing ratios.

rejected_shortcuts: Do not divide total or advertising revenue by any MW figure; Meta does not quantify the incremental AI monetization bridge.
Do not use capex, purchase commitments, lease obligations or residual-value guarantees as revenue.
Do not use 1 GW of future El Paso stated compute capacity as Q2 2026 active IT MW or infer its power boundary.
Do not apply FY2024 fleet PUE to Q2 2026 AI workloads, third-party cloud capacity or future joint-venture campuses.
Do not treat offers to buy compute at a premium as executed contracts or recognized external Meta Compute revenue.
Do not sum lease obligations, contractual commitments, cloud agreements, venture exposure and debt without resolving overlaps and perimeters.

token_economics.reason: Meta disclosed prospective subscription, volume, result-based, API and per-token pricing approaches but no matched realized token price, token/task volume, model mix, energy per token or AI-attributable revenue series.

structured_deals.economic_effect: Approximately $21B for dedicated multi-location AI cloud capacity through December 2032, including initial Vera Rubin deployments. MW, delivery schedule, pricing units, hardware title and take-or-pay details are not public, so no $/MW rate is calculated.

Hyperion has about $27B estimated development cost, 80/20 ownership, a $12.31B initial lease commitment, a declining approximately $28B RVG threshold and $46.03B maximum Meta exposure at June 30, 2026. External capital changes funding timing but Meta remains the intended campus user with substantial lease and residual-value exposure.

El Paso has $14B estimated development cost and $12.5B project debt against 1 GW of stated compute capacity, implying $14.0M development cost and $12.5M debt per stated compute MW. The stated-MW boundary is not defined. Meta will lease the entire campus, may extend to 20 years and provides a declining approximately $13B RVG threshold for the first 16 years.

counterparties: multiple undisclosed lessors, cloud providers and equipment suppliers
structured_deals.economic_effect: Uncommenced leases increased from $103.77B at year-end 2025 to $278.99B at June 30, 2026; Meta added about $68B of data-center leases in July. Noncancelable contractual commitments increased from $131.05B to $349.31B, with another contingent cloud-capacity obligation up to $14.72B. These categories can overlap and are not summed.

findings: No defensible Meta AI revenue per effective utilized IT MW range can be calculated. The exact missing inputs are incremental recognized AI-attributable monetization or recognized external Meta Compute revenue, period-average active AI IT MW and matching physical utilization.
Meta reported FY2024 fleet PUE of 1.08, but it is a historical fleet proxy and not a matched Q2 2026 AI-workload input.

The strongest quantitative finding is the rapid expansion of fixed and quasi-fixed infrastructure obligations: uncommenced leases rose about 169% and noncancelable contractual commitments about 167% from December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026, before the additional approximately $68B July leases.

El Paso illustrates financing intensity rather than operating revenue economics: $14.0M development cost and $12.5M project debt per stated compute MW, with Meta leasing the full campus and providing a residual-value backstop.

Management attributes engagement and advertising performance gains to AI and describes premium external-compute demand, but disclosures do not isolate dollars attributable to AI or recognized Meta Compute revenue.
gaps: Incremental recognized advertising, engagement or productivity value attributable specifically to AI, separated from macro, currency, ad load, users, pricing and non-AI product changes.
Recognized external Meta Compute, API, business-agent and per-token revenue, with pricing, volume, contract duration and revenue-recognition terms.
Opening and daily active AI IT MW by owned, leased, colocated and third-party-cloud cohort; additions, retirements and acceptance dates.
Matching physical utilization and availability definitions for training and inference cohorts.
Current AI-specific PUE, facility and IT energy, and IT-energy weights across owned and third-party cohorts.

Site and hardware allocation for the $278.99B uncommenced leases, $349.31B commitments, $14.72B contingent cloud obligation and July $68B leases, including overlap, termination rights and delivery schedules.
Hardware title, refresh/replacement obligations, useful life, collateral and residual-value allocation within CoreWeave, Hyperion and El Paso arrangements.
Power procurement volumes, tariffs and matching PPA/project financing for AI sites.
Matched realized token prices, task/token volumes and compute-energy series needed for exact Jevons break-even analysis.
